## What students learn

Students identify true series and parallel groups, redraw a mixed circuit, reduce it step by step, solve the equivalent circuit, return to the original branches, and check voltage, current, resistance, and power.

## Why it matters

A reduction plan turns a complicated circuit into smaller problems that can be checked.

## Notes and equations

[Open the Series-Parallel Circuits notes](../../circuits/series-parallel-circuits.qmd)

The website notes use LaTeX for each reduction rule:

\[
R_{\mathrm{series}} = \sum_{k=1}^{n} R_k
\]

\[
\frac{1}{R_{\mathrm{parallel}}} = \sum_{k=1}^{n}\frac{1}{R_k}
\]

After the circuit is reduced, students solve the equivalent circuit and work back to the original branches.

## Learning route

1. Show a complete low-voltage system with one series component and two parallel loads.
2. Watch the conceptual video and identify where current splits.
3. Move from the physical build to the canonical schematic.
4. Trace nodes and identify one reducible group.
5. Redraw after every reduction.
6. Solve one guided GUESS example.
7. Enter each calculator step on a separate line.
8. Complete five progressively harder questions and submit one photo for each.
9. Verify the method with an adaptation of Grob Experiment 6-1.

## Experiment 6-1 adaptation

Use a protected current-limited direct-current supply, breadboard, fused digital multimeter, leads, jumpers, and teacher-selected resistor values. Students submit reduction drawings, calculated and measured resistance, voltage and current checks, percent difference, and one clear circuit photo.

Power must be off for resistance measurements. The ammeter must be connected in series. Do not create a deliberate hard short.

[Open the Grob Experiments Manual](https://drive.google.com/file/d/15KJmGLXvTh0oivaqnV0SvWB7N64V1soT/view){target="_blank"}

Experiment 6-2 is a useful network extension after the core investigation.

## Scope boundary

This package covers reduction and complete analysis. A later package will cover random unknowns, opens, shorts, and troubleshooting. Kirchhoff's laws are a separate unit based on Grob Chapter 9.
